subject: Paperwork inventory and billing trigger clarification
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: John Tucker <john.tucker@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + outstanding paperwork & billing start question

Hi John — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and three items I promised to follow up on: 

1) Procurement path: you mentioned procurement prefers a PO for legal review, but the finance team can also pay by card if we can provide an invoice immediately. Can you confirm which of those two routes you will require for this pilot?

2) Paperwork inventory: attached is a first-pass SOW / statement-of-work draft and a short spreadsheet summarizing payment options (PO vs card vs marketplace). If procurement wants additional fields in the SOW (billing contact, W9, custom data-retention terms), please flag them so we can iterate quickly.

3) Billing trigger: for conversion from free trial to paid, we typically begin billing on the first day the account exceeds the agreed usage threshold or on an agreed calendar date. For planning, can you confirm whether Vertex Health wants billing triggered by (A) usage threshold (e.g., 100k tokens / 30 days) or (B) a specific start date after trial acceptance? If it's (A), what's the acceptance threshold you prefer?

Next steps I propose: I’ll wait for procurement to confirm PO vs card and any SOW edits, then loop in Marcus to finalize pricing details and Laura to schedule paperwork handoff. If you prefer, we can also route via the marketplace for a faster onboarding path — we can provide marketplace SKU IDs in the payment-options spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood-sow-draft-v1.pdf (draft), payment-options-summary.xlsx (one-pager)

Thanks — I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT if you want a short call to walk through procurement details.

—
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0143

From: John Tucker <john.tucker@vertexhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vertexhealth.com, Elena Morales <elena@enterprise.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + outstanding paperwork & billing start question

Priya — great session, thanks. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Procurement path: you mentioned procurement prefers a PO for legal review, but the finance team can also pay by card if we can provide an invoice immediately. Can you confirm which of those two routes you will require for this pilot?

We’d prefer the PO route for the pilot — procurement requires a PO for anything over $10k. I’ve added procurement@vertexhealth.com on this thread to coordinate. If an expedited card payment is needed to unblock the pilot faster, let me know and I’ll see if finance can accept that temporarily, but PO is the primary path.

> 2) Paperwork inventory: attached is a first-pass SOW / statement-of-work draft and a short spreadsheet summarizing payment options (PO vs card vs marketplace). If procurement wants additional fields in the SOW (billing contact, W9, custom data-retention terms), please flag them so we can iterate quickly.

Procurement: we need Redwood’s W9 and preferred billing contact added to the SOW. Also our security team will request a short appendix with data retention and deletion windows — I’ll introduce them if needed.

> 3) Billing trigger: for conversion from free trial to paid, we typically begin billing on the first day the account exceeds the agreed usage threshold or on an agreed calendar date. For planning, can you confirm whether Vertex Health wants billing triggered by (A) usage threshold (e.g., 100k tokens / 30 days) or (B) a specific start date after trial acceptance? If it's (A), what's the acceptance threshold you prefer?

We prefer (A) — convert to paid when the trial usage exceeds the threshold. Tentatively set the threshold at 75k tokens in a rolling 30-day window. If you need a calendar date fallback, set 2027-01-15 as the firm latest start for billing.

I’ll let procurement (cc’d) speak to SOW items and lead times. Thanks, John

John Tucker
VP Product, Vertex Health
john.tucker@vertexhealth.com

From: procurement@vertexhealth.com <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
To: John Tucker <john.tucker@vertexhealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@enterprise.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + outstanding paperwork & billing start question

Hi Priya / John — procurement team here. A few items from our side: 

- PO process: typical lead time is 10 business days from receipt of a signed SOW + vendor W9. If Redwood can accept a provisional PO (we issue a PO number and return the signed SOW upon legal review), we can often accelerate to 4–5 business days.

- Required paperwork: W9 (PDF), vendor contact email for remittance, standard insurance certificiates (if applicable). For the SOW we need a billing contact name, billing address, and tax info section included.

- Marketplace: we can take marketplace purchases but prefer direct PO for internal tracking. If Redwood can provide marketplace SKU + pricing guarantee for 90 days, we’ll consider that as alternative.

Please send a W9 and a revised SOW with the billing contact block filled. If you want the provisional PO route, confirm and we’ll issue a PO number today.

Thanks — Procurement Ops
procurement@vertexhealth.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@vertexhealth.com, John Tucker <john.tucker@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + outstanding paperwork & billing start question

Thanks — quick internal note and proposal (forwarding to Marcus + Laura to action): 

(Quoted) 
On Mon, 30 Nov 2026 at 11:03 procurement@vertexhealth.com wrote:
> If Redwood can accept a provisional PO (we issue a PO number and return the signed SOW upon legal review), we can often accelerate to 4–5 business days.

Proposed Redwood response and next steps: 
- We can accept a provisional PO. If procurement issues a PO number now, Redwood will: (a) accept the provisional PO to reserve capacity and pricing; (b) issue an invoice against the PO once SOW is signed; (c) start trial-to-paid billing based on the agreed usage threshold (75k tokens / rolling 30d) OR the fallback date 2027-01-15 if threshold isn't reached earlier.
- Action items for Marcus: confirm the pricing floor in the SOW matches the pilot pricing and prepare a one-page invoice template that can be issued against a PO number. (Attachment: payment-options-summary.xlsx)
- Action items for Laura: prepare a W9 and fill the billing contact block in the SOW; return revised SOW to procurement@vertexhealth.com and cc John.

I’ll also add a short clause proposal to the SOW around billing trigger language: "Billing will commence on the earlier of (i) the date on which cumulative billable usage exceeds 75,000 tokens in any 30-day window, or (ii) January 15, 2027." If there are objections from legal, we can take the clause to your legal counsel for redlines.

Marcus / Laura — can you action the two items above today so we can accept a provisional PO this week? John — appreciate if you can nudge procurement if helpful.

Thanks — Priya
